basis: Intellectual disability and skin hyperpigmentation define the syndrome; hypotonia alone does not establish primary muscle disease.
Malignant mesenchymal soft-tissue tumour, usually retroperitoneal; adjacent-organ invasion is not universal.
Inherited metabolic defects directly impair skeletal muscle; other organs vary across the umbrella.
Persistent disease of multiple peripheral nerves; no shared systemic mechanism across subtypes.
Persistent nerve injury following herpes zoster; residual neuralgia does not itself establish ongoing infection or skin disease.
Contractures and skin hyalinosis define disease; GI malabsorption and immunodeficiency each 80–99%. Adrenal abnormalities lack demonstrated functional damage.
Adenoviral infection defined by pharyngitis and conjunctivitis; both are primary sites of inflammation.
Congenital cardiac defects and brain abnormalities characterize syndrome; hand abnormalities 80–99%, contractures 30–79%. Renal anomaly frequency unspecified.
Usually arises in placental or reproductive tissue, outside the axes; pulmonary metastases are separately diagnosed secondary malignancy.
B-cell developmental immunodeficiency with agammaglobulinemia; associated otitis, pneumonia and meningitis are separate infections.
Molecular subtype of a primary central nervous system tumour.
Arterial dysplasia defines disease; joint subluxation 3/6 and atrophic skin scars 2/6 support structural involvement. Migraine does not establish brain injury.
Inherited bile-acid metabolism disorder; clinically significant liver injury is not established across this heterogeneous umbrella.
Inherited Alzheimer disease causes progressive cerebral neurodegeneration.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; no extra-auditory disease established.
Inherited marrow failure with aplasia or myelodysplasia; sensorineural hearing impairment occurs in 4/6 patients.
Purine disorder with defining neurologic dysfunction; nephrocalcinosis 13/17, renal insufficiency and anemia 30–79%. Gout is separately diagnosed.
Benign epithelial neoplasm arising in bronchial or pulmonary tissue.
Alkaline-phosphatase deficiency defined by defective skeletal mineralization, fractures and dental abnormalities; teeth belong to gastrointestinal.
Surfactant deficiency causes alveolar collapse and impaired pulmonary gas exchange.
Wolfram phenotype includes diabetes, optic atrophy and deafness; neurologic degeneration occurs in >30%. Urinary abnormalities omitted by cap; subtype frequencies uncertain.
Recurrent hereditary brachial plexus axonal neuropathy; muscle weakness and atrophy result from denervation rather than primary muscle disease.
Congenital neutrophil maturation failure causes severe neutropenia and innate immunodeficiency; resulting infections are separate diseases.
Degenerative cerebellar disorder; supplied HPO reports macular degeneration and visual loss in 30–79%, supporting direct ocular involvement beyond abnormal eye movements.
Neurodevelopmental disease with agammaglobulinemia; optic atrophy 2/4 and central hypothyroidism 1/1 assessed. Respiratory failure lacks evidence of direct lung injury.
